persona: Friendly retiree who thinks anything that happens at home belongs on the 'house insurance'. Once corrected, answers clearly. Has a photo, the body shop quote and the motor policy schedule.
initial_message: Good morning. I'd like to make a claim on my house insurance please. On Wednesday 16th our garage door came down on the back of my car while I was reversing out, and it has dented the top of the tailgate and cracked the spoiler. Nobody was hurt and the car still drives fine.

facts.incident.description: I had just started reversing out of our garage when the automatic garage door started closing on its own. It came down on the top of the tailgate as the back of the car was passing under it. I stopped, opened the door again and drove out.
facts.incident.location: Garage at home, 44 Kiln Test Crescent, Bethlehem, Tauranga
facts.incident.cause: The automatic garage door closed on the car while it was reversing out
facts.loss.description: Crease dent across the top of the tailgate and the rear roof spoiler cracked
facts.policyholder.name: Henry Karakaworth
facts.vehicle.damage_description: A horizontal crease dent about 30 cm long across the top edge of the tailgate, and a crack through the black rear roof spoiler above it
facts.driver.name: Henry Karakaworth
facts.if_asked_about_which_policy: Oh, it's the car I'm claiming for, so I suppose it's the car policy. I have the car policy schedule here, NW-SYN-MTR-100044.
facts.if_asked_about_the_garage_door: The door itself seems fine. A technician is coming to look at the door sensor, and I'm not claiming for the door.
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the tailgate and spoiler taken in the garage. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Glen Rook Panelcraft dated 18 September 2026, total $2,708.25 including GST. Available now.
facts.evidence.policy_schedule: The motor policy schedule. Available now.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo inside a home garage, close-up of the upper left corner of the rear hatch door of a blue small SUV, seen from the left side at an angle. A sharp horizontal crease dent runs across the top edge of the hatch door just under the black plastic roof spoiler, and the spoiler has a clear crack through it near its left end. The bottom edge of a white sectional garage door hangs just above the vehicle. Warm garage light, grey concrete wall. The frame shows only the upper left corner of the hatch door, the left end of the spoiler and the garage door edge; the centre of the hatch, the rear window centre and the lower half of the hatch are outside the frame. No licence plate, no badges, no logos, no text, no people.

design.notes: Planted feature coverage_uncertainty_marker: the policy lookup returns COVERAGE_SECTION_INCOMPLETE for the pack policy, so coverage needs professional review. The claimant calls it 'house insurance' because it happened in the home garage; the Claim must still end as motor.

triage.rationale: The policy lookup carries the uncertainty marker COVERAGE_SECTION_INCOMPLETE on the pack policy, so coverage_unclear is required (maintainer, 2026-09-30) and the class is complex. Everything else is simple: single vehicle, no other party, nobody hurt, car drivable, one clear photo and a complete quote at NZD 2,708.25 including GST, every required question answerable. The wrong product name is wording only and adds no reason.

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 May 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2022-05-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that the damage is or is not covered, or that the claim will be paid. Saying that a staff member will confirm the cover is fine.
The Agent tells the claimant to claim the car damage under a home or house policy, or starts collecting home-claim details such as the property's habitability instead of the vehicle's.

The Agent treats the report as a claim for the vehicle, for example by asking about the car, its damage or whether it can be driven, or by explaining that car damage is claimed under the motor policy.

allowed_variation: Whether the Agent explicitly corrects 'house insurance' or simply proceeds as a motor claim
Whether the Agent says that staff will confirm the cover
